raw_refs.value: [1] Although the word is recent, the idea of decoherence goes back at least to G. Ludwig (Z. f. Physik 135, 483 (1953), 150, 346 (1958), and 152, 98 (1958). Some other early papers, concentrating on the role of the environment in the measurement problem, are H.S. Green, Nuovo Cim. 9, 880 (1958); A. Daneri, A. Loinger, GM Prosperi, Nucl. Phys. 33, 297 (1962), and Nuovo Cim. 44B, 119 (1966); H.D. Zeh, Found. Phys. 1, 69 (1970), and M Simonius, Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 980 (1978). These papers were all rather qualititative, but argued that environmental correlations would destroy large-scale quantum behaviour.

raw_refs.value: [13] One can attempt to rewrite the Fractional Hall Hamiltonian so that interactions are partially incorporated into the bare Hamiltonian (for example in the composite fermion gauge theory- see B.I. Halperin, P.A.Lee, N. Read, Phys. Rev. B47, 7312 (1993)). However the problem of Landau level degeneracy is not so easily finessed- it reappears in the form of severe infra-red divergences in the renormalised interactions, which have to be dealt with non-perturbatively (see, eg., J. Polchinski, Nucl. Phys. B422, 617 (1994); D. Khveschenko, P.C.E. Stamp, Phys. Rev. Lett. 71, 4226 (1993); D.V. Khveschenko, P.C.E. Stamp, Pys. Rev B49, 5227 (1994); Y.B. Kim et al., Phys. Rev B50, 17917 (1994); B.L. Altshuler, L.B.Ioffe, A.J. Millis, Phys. Rev. 50, 14048 (1994); C. Nayak, F. Wilczek, Nucl. Phys. B417, 359 (1994), and Nucl. Phys. B430, 534 (1994); Y.B. Kim, X.G. Wen, P.A. Lee, P.C.E. Stamp, Phys Rev. B51, 10779 (1995); A. Stern, B.I. Halperin, Phys. Rev. B48, 17368 (1995)). As yet there is no solution to this non-perturbative behaviour- different methods give different answers.

abstracts.value: We briefly review the oscillator and spin bath models of quantum environments, which can be used to describe the low-energy dynamics of open quantum systems. We then use them to discuss both the mechanisms causing decoherence at low $T$, and the dynamics of this decoherence. This is done first for a central 2-level system coupled to these environments- the results can be applied to the dynamics of quantum nanomagnets and superconducting SQUIDs, where large-scale tunneling of magnetisation and flux take place. Decoherence in these systems is caused principally by coupling to electrons and nuclear spins, the spin bath couplings are particularly dangerous at low $T$. These models are also generalised to discuss quantum measurements in which the measured system, the measuring apparatus, and the environment are treated quantum mechanically. The results can be used to calculate the dynamics of coupled SQUIDs and/or nanomagnets, in which one acts as a measuring apparatus and the other exhibits large-scale quantum superpositions. The same model can be used to describe coupled qubits.

titles.title: Mechanisms of Decoherence at Low Temperatures
